archetypes.name: loop-integration
archetypes.rationale: The diff introduces a dual-status system (STEP3_REVIEW_LOOP_STATUS + LOOP_STATUS) with bridge mapping logic in SKILL.md; coexistence gaps or misrouted bail-outs could silently misdirect apply/continuation paths.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine how SKILL.md bridges STEP3_REVIEW_LOOP_STATUS to the legacy LOOP_STATUS variable in the post-loop branch matrix. Verify that every STEP3_REVIEW_LOOP_STATUS enum value (complete, cap-hit, main-agent-vote-required, main-agent-apply-required, per-round-approval-required, postplan-operator-required, postplan-failed, panel-failed, tally-error, degraded-empty-collector) has a correct and complete mapping and that no enum value can fall through to the legacy LOOP_STATUS path unintentionally. Check whether callers that read only LOOP_STATUS (harnesses, test-step3-orchestrator-fence.sh, test-design-structure.sh) will remain correct when STEP3_REVIEW_LOOP_STATUS is set — specifically whether legacy --mode single callers and new loop callers can coexist without the wrong branch being taken. Also verify that the run-params.json approve_requested field is correctly read in both mode paths (the old APPROVE_REQUESTED fence and the new loop's per-round-approval-required bail-out) and that mismatches between the two reads cannot produce inconsistent apply behavior. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: phase-marker-consistency
archetypes.rationale: A new three-state per-round phase marker (.step3-round-N.phase) drives exact-once apply and resume routing; inconsistent transitions across dedup-failure, postplan rc 11, and main-agent-apply-required paths could cause double-apply or skipped plan revision.
archetypes.prompt_body: Focus on the .step3-round-N.phase state machine defined across review-design-step3-loop.sh and SKILL.md. For each of the three states (awaiting-apply, awaiting-post-apply, awaiting-continuation), verify that every code path writes the marker at the documented moment — specifically: that awaiting-post-apply is written immediately after successful reviser apply and before dedup/postplan (not after); that a dedup failure correctly restores the loop snapshot and bails out without promoting the phase; that postplan rc 11 (in-loop pause-save) leaves the phase at awaiting-post-apply rather than promoting it; and that .gate-b-postapply-ready-N is written only after dedup succeeds. Check whether design-step3-state.sh's settled lower-round cleanup (--direct-review-entry) could race with a concurrent resume that still needs the marker for its round, and whether the cleanup correctly distinguishes settled lower-round markers from the live round's marker. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
